Spin gap Δ_s ≈ 5.5 from NMR (the rung singlet→triplet gap; model: 4.7–5.0). Single-particle gap E_g = 7.9. Transport gap E_g/2 ≈ 3.7–4.0. |\n14\t| **1. Effective theory** | A one-orbital **bilayer Hubbard–Heisenberg model** on the bilayer square lattice, with one rung (2 TM sites) per primitive cell: H = −t Σ c†c (nn, in plane) − t′ Σ c†c (nnn, in plane) − t⊥ Σ c†c (rung) + U Σ n↑n↓ + J⊥ Σ (S₁·S₂ − n₁n₂/4) − μN. Values: **t = 1.00 ± 0.02**, **t′ = +0.20 ± 0.02**, **\\|t⊥\\| < 0.2**, **U = 1.4 ± 0.8**, **J⊥ = 6.6 ± 0.5**. It conserves charge (separately per layer when t⊥ = 0), SU(2) spin, time reversal, translations and D4h. It lacks particle–hole symmetry (t′), the η-pseudospin SU(2), and any Lieb–Schultz–Mattis obstruction (two electrons per cell at ν = 1/2). |\n15\t| **2. Phase diagram** | Band insulators at ν = 0, 1. Interlayer s± superconducting domes on both sides of ν = 1/2, with T_c bounded by the mean-field pairing scale T_MF(ν) and driven to zero at ν = 1/2. There the rung pairs fill every rung and localize, giving the rung-singlet insulator. A preformed-pair (pseudogap) regime lies between T_c and T*, and a normal metal above. Low → high T: **ν = 1/2**: rung-singlet insulator → (T ≳ 5) correlated paramagnet / bad metal. **ν ≈ 0.3**: s± superconductor (T < 0.36) → preformed rung pairs, pseudogap, insulating-like (0.36 < T < 2.5–3) → normal metal. **ν ≈ 0.2**: BCS-like s± superconductor (T < 1.11) → normal Fermi-liquid metal. |\n16\t| **3. Data explained** | See the table in §5: every feature maps onto one ingredient of the model. |\n17\t| **4. ARPES** | **ν = 1/2:** two rigidly translated, half-width bands (ε_k/2 ± E_ex/2); indirect gap from M (top of the lower band, −4) to Γ (bottom of the upper band, +4); no replica bands. **ν ≈ 0.3:** Bogoliubov back-bending at k_F with Δ ≈ 2.9, plus a second, local pairing scale ≈ 5.2 away from k_F. **ν ≈ 0.2:** sharp BCS Bogoliubov bands with Δ ≈ 2.0 on the bare band. |\n18\t| **5. Zeros of G at ω = 0, ν = 1/2** | A small **closed curve around M = (½,½)**. The side containing Γ covers **0.85 ± 0.03 of the Brillouin zone** (16-site CPT: 0.855; 8 → 12 → 16 sites: 0.914 → 0.871 → 0.855), compared with ν = 0.5, so Luttinger's theorem written with zeros fails. The cause is particle–hole asymmetry (t′ ≠ 0): the zeros form a narrow band centred about 0.25 above the midgap chemical potential (2t′ at first order), so μ cuts it only near M. Control calculation: with t′ = 0 the same method gives exactly 0.50. |\n19\t\n20\t---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n21\t\n22\t## 1. What the measurements say before any model is chosen\n23\t\n24\t### 1.1 Band structure (STS, Fig. 1(d), high T)\n25\t\n26\tA least-squares fit of panel (d) to the density of states of\n27\tε_k = −2t(cos k_x + cos k_y) − 4t′ cos k_x cos k_y, with filling ν, a Gaussian resolution and a smooth\n28\tbackground, gives:\n29\t\n30\t* **t = 1.000 ± 0.004 (stat.) ± 0.02 (syst.)**, i.e. D is the nearest-neighbour hopping\n31\t* **t′ = 0.195 ± 0.002 (stat.) ± 0.02 (syst.)**\n32\t* **ν = 0.300 ± 0.001**\n33\t\n34\tThe band edges (−4.0, +4.2 relative to μ) and the van Hove peak at +1.75 are reproduced to within 0.05. t′ > 0 in\n35\tthis sign convention puts the van Hove singularity above the band centre and the band bottom at Γ. There\n36\tis no second van Hove peak, which bounds a bonding–antibonding splitting at 2|t⊥| ≲ 0.3.\n37\t\n38\t### 1.2 The half-filled crystal\n39\t\n40\t1. **Hubbard-like split bands.** The two bands in Fig. 1(a) are *rigid translates* of each other. Their\n41\t   overlap after a shift of 12.1 ± 0.1 is 0.976; the overlap of the mirror image is only 0.70. Each band is\n42\t   4.0 wide, i.e. half the bare bandwidth 8t. A superconducting gap would make the spectrum mirror-symmetric\n43\t   about μ (Bogoliubov poles at ±E_k), so this is **not** a pairing gap of a condensate.\n44\t2. **Spectral weights.** The weight below the gap is 0.50 (= ν). The lower band is weighted toward its bottom\n45\t   (states near Γ) and the upper band toward its top (states near M). The ratio follows\n46\t   Z∓ = ½ ∓ ε_k/(2E_ex) with E_ex ≈ 12, the strong-coupling (Hubbard-I-type) form.\n47\t3. **Gaps.** The single-particle gap is E_g = 7.9 ± 0.1 (edges at ±3.95). The resistivity is activated with\n48\t   Δ_ρ = 3.72 ± 0.05 ≈ E_g/2, as for an intrinsic semiconductor with μ at midgap.\n49\t4. **Spin gap.** 1/(T₁T) falls by five decades between T = 4.4 and 0.45. It is a pure exponential with\n50\t   Δ_s = 5.5 ± 0.5 (a free power-law prefactor T^p fits to p = −0.04 ± 0.38). The STS density of states alone\n51\t   would give an activation of only 3.75 (Korringa estimate from Fig. 1(a)). **Spin excitations therefore cost\n52\t   more than the thermal charge carriers**: Δ_s = 5.5 > Δ_ρ = 3.7, with Δ_s < E_g = 7.9.\n53\t5. **No broken symmetry.** There are no new or split diffraction peaks, all TM sites are equivalent, the TM NMR\n54\t   line is single, and STS is the same everywhere.\n55\t\n56\t**Lieb–Schultz–Mattis (LSM) constraint.** At ν = 1/2 each TM carries one electron. If the primitive cell\n57\tcontained one TM, the LSM–Oshikawa–Hastings theorem would forbid a unique, gapped, fully symmetric ground state.\n58\tThe only way out would be topological order, with gaps bounded by the exchange scale (≈ 4t²/U ≈ 0.3), far below\n59\tthe measured 5.5 and 3.7. The data therefore require **an even number of electrons per primitive cell**, i.e. two\n60\tcrystallographically equivalent TM sites per cell. This is exactly what a perovskite **bilayer** block provides\n61\t(two TMO₂ planes sharing apical oxygens, related by a mirror plane). It is compatible with every structural\n62\tstatement: in-plane period a, all TM equivalent, one NMR line.\n63\t\n64\t### 1.3 The doped crystals\n65\t\n66\t* **ν ≈ 0.2.** Panel (c) is BCS on the bare band: **Δ = 1.964 ± 0.002**, with μ equal to the normal-state value\n67\t  μ₀(0.2) = −1.92 (fit −1.922 ± 0.004), so the underlying Fermi surface encloses exactly ν. The NMR shows a\n68\t  Hebel–Slichter peak (1.7× the normal value at T ≈ 0.8–1.0) and is fitted by BCS with Δ(0) = 1.98 and\n69\t  **T_c = 1.11** (2Δ/T_c = 3.6). The resistivity is metallic and vanishes below T_c = 1.11 ± 0.04. Pairing is\n70\t  s-wave-like (full gap, coherence peak) and weak-coupling.\n71\t* **ν ≈ 0.3.** There is a hard gap, but no single BCS gap fits (rms 0.16). Panel (b) needs an energy-dependent\n72\t  gap: **Δ₀ = 2.85 ± 0.02** at the Fermi surface, rising to **Δ_∞ = 5.23** for |ξ_k| ≳ 1 (rms 0.034). That\n73\t  second scale matches the half-filled spin gap. The NMR gap is 2.7 ± 0.1 both above and below\n74\t  **T_c = 0.36 ± 0.04** and opens at T* ≈ 2.5–3. The normal state is insulating-like (ρ ∝ e^{0.9/T}).\n75\t  This is a strongly paired superconductor with preformed pairs, where T_c ≪ Δ.\n76\t* **Trend toward ν = 1/2.** The gap grows (1.96 → 2.85 → 3.95), T_c falls (1.11 → 0.36 → 0) and coherence is\n77\t  lost. This is the doping evolution of a Mott insulator, here one of *pairs*.\n78\t\n79\t---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n80\t\n81\t## 2. Why the standard single-layer models fail (and the bilayer does not)\n82\t\n83\t| Candidate | Fatal problem (quantified) |\n84\t|---|---|\n85\t| Repulsive one-layer Hubbard, U ≈ 12 | Local moments with J = 4t²/U ≈ 0.33: 1/T₁ would be roughly constant (1/T₁T rising) for T ≫ J, against the observed five-decade activated drop. A spin gap of 5.5 ≫ J is impossible. It also gives d-wave nodal pairing, not a full gap with a Hebel–Slichter peak. |\n86\t| Attractive one-layer Hubbard, U ≈ −12 (fixes Fig. 1(a) and Δ_s ≈ \\|U\\|/2) | (i) **Exact diagonalization** (10, 16, 20-site clusters) gives single-particle gaps of 3.4–3.6 at ν ≈ 0.2 and 3.7–4.0 at ν ≈ 0.3, versus 1.96 and 2.85 measured. The gap decreases toward the two-body value E_b/2 = 2.06 only as ν → 0 (2.5–2.6 for a single pair on 16–20 sites). (ii) Spin and charge excitations are the same quasiparticles, so it cannot give Δ_s > Δ_ρ. (iii) Pairs hop with J ≈ 4t²/\\|U\\| ≈ 0.33 and would conduct for T ≫ J, so ρ(0.45)/ρ(4) ≈ 1, not 1600. (iv) At fixed U, lower density is *more* BEC-like, the opposite of the trend. (v) The high-T spectrum at ν = 0.3 would carry Hubbard satellites holding 30% of the weight; they are absent in Fig. 1(d). |\n87\t| One layer, topological spin liquid | Allowed by LSM, but its gaps are bounded by ~J ≈ 0.3, not 5.5. |\n88\t| **Bilayer, strong interlayer singlet coupling J⊥, small U, t⊥ ≈ 0** | Explains every item quantitatively (§5). It is LSM-allowed: two electrons per primitive cell at ν = 1/2. |\n89\t\n90\t![model selection](figures/fig6_model_selection.png)\n91\t\n92\t*Fig. 6.* (a) Single-particle half-gap versus filling. The attractive single-layer model (ED on 10, 16 and 20\n93\tsites) stays near 3.4–4.2 at every filling. The bilayer model gives 2.45, 2.70 and 4.10 at ν = 0.19, 0.31, 0.5\n94\t(ED), and its J⊥ mean field gives 1.98 at ν = 0.2. Measured: 1.96, 2.6–2.85, 3.95. (b) At ν = ½ only the bilayer\n95\treproduces the ordering *spin gap > thermal charge gap* seen in NMR versus resistivity.\n96\t\n97\t---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n98\t\n99\t## 3. Task 1 — the effective theory\n100\t\n101\t**Degrees of freedom.** Spin-½ electrons in the single active orbital of each TM. This is a d_{x²−y²}-like\n102\torbital σ-bonded to the in-plane oxygens. Its O admixture is what makes the hopping range reach t′, and its\n103\tapical-O / d_{z²} admixture is what transmits the interlayer exchange. Each site has four states: empty, ↑, ↓\n104\tand doubly occupied.\n105\t\n106\t**Lattice and unit cell.** The bilayer square lattice. A site is labelled (i, l): i runs over an in-plane square\n107\tlattice with constant a, and l = 1, 2 labels the two planes of one perovskite block. The primitive cell is one\n108\t**rung**, i.e. the two TM sites stacked along c, related by the mirror plane between the layers. The Brillouin\n109\tzone is the in-plane square zone. ν = 1/2 means two electrons per primitive cell.\n110\t\n111\t**Hamiltonian** (every term):\n112\t\n113\t```\n114\tH = − t   Σ_{⟨ij⟩, l, σ}  ( c†_{ilσ} c_{jlσ} + h.c. )          in-plane nearest-neighbour hopping\n115\t    − t′  Σ_{⟨⟨ij⟩⟩, l, σ} ( c†_{ilσ} c_{jlσ} + h.c. )          in-plane next-nearest-neighbour hopping\n116\t    − t⊥  Σ_{i, σ}         ( c†_{i1σ} c_{i2σ} + h.c. )          interlayer (rung) hopping\n117\t    + U   Σ_{i, l}          n_{il↑} n_{il↓}                     on-site Coulomb repulsion\n118\t    + J⊥  Σ_i              ( S_{i1}·S_{i2} − ¼ n_{i1} n_{i2} )  interlayer (rung) singlet exchange\n119\t    − μ   Σ_{i, l}          n_{il}                              chemical potential (sets ν)\n120\t```\n121\t\n122\tso that ε_k = −2t(cos k_x + cos k_y) − 4t′ cos k_x cos k_y (k in units of 1/a) within each layer.\n123\t\n124\t**Coefficients and how they were determined.**\n125\t\n126\t| Coefficient | Value | Uncertainty | Determined from |\n127\t|---|---|---|---|\n128\t| t | 1.00 | ± 0.02 | fit of the high-T STS (d): band edges and van Hove peak; consistent with (a) and (c) |\n129\t| t′ | +0.20 | ± 0.02 | same fit (van Hove peak 1.75 above μ, asymmetric band edges); χ² profile minimum at 0.20 |\n130\t| t⊥ | 0 | \\|t⊥\\| < 0.2 | no bonding–antibonding splitting of the van Hove peak in (d), resolution 0.14 |\n131\t| J⊥ | 6.6 | ± 0.5 | (i) half-filled NMR spin gap 5.5 ± 0.5 = triplon gap ≈ J⊥ − (1.4 to 1.8) (ED, 16-site bilayer) → J⊥ = 7.1 ± 0.6; (ii) BCS gap at ν ≈ 0.2: Δ = 1.96 requires J⊥ = 6.5 in mean field; (iii) T_c(0.2) = 1.11 = T_MF requires J⊥ = 6.45; (iv) ED doped gaps prefer 5.5–6.5. Weighted combination. |\n132\t| U | 1.4 | ± 0.8 | half-filled single-particle gap: E_g/2 = 3.95 = U/2 + 3J⊥/4 − (1.69 ± 0.03), the last term from band broadening (ED); uncertainty dominated by J⊥. The splitting between Hubbard-band centres, 12.1 ≈ U + 3J⊥/2 + O(t²), and the bare band at ν ≤ 0.3 (Fig. 1(c,d)), which requires U ≲ W/2, are consistent. |\n133\t| μ | sets ν | — | μ(ν) |\n134\t\n135\tExact diagonalization of the final parameter set (U = 1.8, J⊥ = 6.5) on the 16-site bilayer gives\n136\ta single-particle half-gap of **4.10** (data 3.95) and a spin gap of **4.72** (data 5.5 ± 0.5). The pair stiffness from twisted boundary conditions is D = 1.06 per rung at ν = 0.19, 0.74 at ν = 0.31 and 0.02 at ν = ½, i.e. 75%, 42% and 1% of the free-electron value. The other runs give (half-gap / spin gap): (U, J⊥) = (3.85, 5.5): 4.33 / 4.13; (3.0, 5.5): 3.96 / 3.97; (1.4, 6.9): 4.18 / 5.02. At fixed charge gap the spin gap rises with J⊥ and reaches the NMR value 5.5 at J⊥ ≈ 7.5, where the doped gaps and T_c(0.2) would come out ≈ 15% too high. J⊥ = 6.6 ± 0.5 balances these constraints.\n137\t\n138\t*Stability of the half-filled state.* The in-plane superexchange through the rung-singlet background is\n139\tJ_∥ ≈ 4t²/E_ex ≈ 0.35, so J⊥/J_∥ ≈ 19. That lies far inside the rung-singlet (quantum-disordered) phase of the\n140\tbilayer Heisenberg model, whose critical ratio is 2.52, so no in-plane antiferromagnetism develops. A\n141\tcharge-density wave would have to break rung singlets (cost ≈ J⊥ per rung), so none develops either. At exactly\n142\tν = ½ every rung holds one pair, which cannot move without creating an empty and a doubly occupied rung (cost\n143\t2U + J⊥ in the atomic limit), so there is no superconductivity.\n144\t\n145\t**Symmetries the model has**\n146\t\n147\t* U(1) charge. For t⊥ = 0 the charge of *each layer* is separately conserved, an extra U(1).\n148\t* SU(2) spin rotation (no spin–orbit term).\n149\t* Time reversal.\n150\t* Translations of the square lattice (one rung per cell).\n151\t* The full point group D4h of a perovskite bilayer: C₄ about c, vertical mirrors, the horizontal mirror σ_h\n152\t  exchanging the layers, and inversion through the rung centre.\n153\t\n154\t**Symmetries the model lacks**\n155\t\n156\t* **Particle–hole symmetry.** t′ ≠ 0, while the U and J⊥ terms are particle–hole symmetric only up to a shift\n157\t  of μ. Consequences: the van Hove peak lies above mid-band; the half-filled spectrum is not mirror-symmetric\n158\t  about its centre; the Green's-function zero is not pinned to μ (Task 5); and the phase diagram is asymmetric\n159\t  about ν = ½.\n160\t* **η-pseudospin (charge) SU(2)**, broken by t′ and by the density part of the J⊥ term. Charge order and pairing are not degenerate.\n161\t* **An LSM obstruction.** Two electrons per cell at ν = ½ permit a unique gapped symmetric ground state. This is\n162\t  why the half-filled insulator can be featureless *without* topological order.\n163\t* **Interlayer band coherence.** t⊥ ≈ 0, so there is no bonding–antibonding splitting.\n164\t* No spin–orbit coupling, no disorder, and no term that doubles the cell.\n165\t\n166\t---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n167\t\n168\t## 4. Task 2 — phase diagram\n169\t\n170\t![phase diagram](figures/fig3_phase_diagram.png)\n171\t\n172\t**How it was obtained** (approximations stated):\n173\t\n174\t* **T_MF(ν):** BCS mean-field onset of interlayer singlet pairing driven by J⊥ (gap equation\n175\t  1 = J⊥ N⁻¹Σ_k tanh(E_k/2T)/2E_k at fixed ν, 256×256 k-grid). It is a broad dome peaking at ν ≈ 0.5–0.55,\n176\t  near the van Hove filling, and is an *upper bound* for T_c.\n177\t* **Rung-singlet regime near ν = ½:** the local singlet–triplet splitting (ED spin gap ≈ 5) sets a\n178\t  crossover T_s ≈ Δ_s/ln 3 ≈ 5 below which every rung is a singlet. At exactly ν = ½ the pairs fill all rungs,\n179\t  their motion is blocked, the pair stiffness collapses (ED, twisted boundaries: its coherent fraction D/D_free falls from 0.75 at ν = 0.19 to 0.42 at ν = 0.31 and to 0.013 at ν = ½, where D = 0.02 per rung), and the state\n180\t  is the rung-singlet insulator.\n181\t* **T_c(ν):** T_c = T_MF(ν) · min[1, (Z(ν)/Z(0.2))^p], with Z = D/D_free the coherent fraction of the pair\n182\t  stiffness from ED (0.75 at ν = 0.19, 0.42 at ν = 0.31, 0.013 at ν = ½). The single exponent\n183\t  p = 2.8 is fixed by the measured T_c(0.3) = 0.36; T_c(0.2) = T_MF = 1.13 then follows. This is an\n184\t  interpolation, not a calculation of T_c. A strictly 2D model would cap T_c at T_KT ≲ 0.3; the measured,\n185\t  mean-field-like T_c implies coupling between bilayers. T_c → 0 for ν → 0 (dilute BCS) and ν → ½ (Mott\n186\t  localization of rung pairs). The ν > ½ side follows from the particle–hole transform (ν → 1−ν, t′ → −t′),\n187\t  which T_MF includes; Z is mirrored.\n188\t* The crossover line T* and the precise dome shape between the measured points are **schematic**. The\n189\t  computed objects are T_MF, the rung-singlet scale, and the vanishing stiffness at ν = ½.\n190\t\n191\t**Phases of each crystal, from low to high temperature**\n192\t\n193\t| Crystal | Phases |\n194\t|---|---|\n195\t| ν = 1/2 | rung-singlet insulator (no broken symmetry; gaps Δ_s ≈ 5.5, E_g ≈ 7.9) up to T_s ≈ 5 → crossover to a correlated paramagnetic bad metal / semiconductor |\n196\t| ν ≈ 0.3 | interlayer s± superconductor (T < 0.36) → preformed rung pairs: pseudogap, spin gap 2.7, insulating-like ρ (0.36 < T < T* ≈ 2.5–3) → normal metal (T ≳ 3) |\n197\t| ν ≈ 0.2 | interlayer s± superconductor, BCS-like (T < 1.11) → normal Fermi-liquid metal (T > 1.11; T* = T_c) |\n198\t\n199\t---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n200\t\n201\t## 5. Task 3 — how the theory produces each set of measurements\n202\t\n203\t![STS vs theory](figures/fig1_sts_vs_theory.png)\n204\t![NMR and resistivity](figures/fig2_nmr_rho_fits.png)\n205\t\n206\t| Measurement | Observation | Feature of the theory that produces it |\n207\t|---|---|---|\n208\t| **Diffraction** | period a, all TM equivalent, no new or split peaks down to the lowest T | The ν = ½ ground state is a product of rung singlets (dressed by virtual hopping). It is unique and invariant under all lattice symmetries, so no superlattice is needed. With two TM per cell the gap needs no symmetry breaking (LSM satisfied). Pairs on the doped side are interlayer, uniform and s-wave. |\n209\t| **NMR line** | single TM line | Both TM of a rung are equivalent by σ_h. There are no ordered moments (singlets) and no charge disproportionation. |\n210\t| **STS (a), ν = ½** | hard gap 7.9; two bands 4.0 wide, rigidly shifted by 12.1; weight 0.50 below | Removing an electron leaves a singly occupied rung (cost ≈ J⊥). Adding one makes a three-electron rung (cost ≈ U + J⊥/2). Both excitations hop through the singlet background with amplitude t/2 (the overlap of a moved electron with a rung singlet). This gives E_±(k) ≈ ±E_ex/2 + ε_k/2, bands of width W/2 and weights ½ ∓ ε_k/(2E_ex). Here E_ex = U + 3J⊥/2 ≈ 11.3, plus ≈ 0.6 of second-order level repulsion, which reproduces the measured splitting 12.1. The gap is E_ex − 3.4 ≈ 7.9 (ED on 16 sites: 8.2). CPT reproduces positions and edges (Fig. 1(a)). |\n211\t| **STS (b), ν ≈ 0.3** | gap 2.6–2.85 at E_F; peaks at ±5.1, edges at ±6.5 | Doping makes rung pairs mobile and they condense. Near k_F the coherent Bogoliubov gap is Δ₀ ≈ 2.85 (mean field: 2.4–2.65). Far from k_F the states still feel the *local* rung-singlet binding ≈ 5.2. The result is a two-scale gap Δ(ξ). |\n212\t| **STS (c), ν ≈ 0.2** | BCS: Δ = 1.96, coherence peaks, bare band | Weak-coupling interlayer s± BCS state on the bare band: Δ = 1.98 for J⊥ = 6.5, with the underlying Fermi surface enclosing ν. U is small, so the band is unrenormalized. |\n213\t| **STS (d), ν ≈ 0.3, high T** | bare t-t′ band, ν = 0.30 | Above all pairing scales the model is a weakly correlated metal (U ≲ W/2, t⊥ ≈ 0): one band per layer, no Hubbard satellites. |\n214\t| **NMR ν = ½** | activated, Δ_s = 5.5 | The rung singlet → triplet gap J⊥ − (triplon dispersion): 4.7 for (U, J⊥) = (1.8, 6.5), 1.5σ below the measured 5.5 ± 0.5. Thermal triplons relax the nucleus. Spin and charge gaps are distinct objects here (singlet–triplet vs. single-particle), which is why Δ_s ≠ Δ_ρ. |\n215\t| **NMR ν ≈ 0.3** | activated, 2.7, unchanged across T_c, onset at T* ≈ 2.5–3 | Preformed rung pairs. The quasiparticle gap opens at T*, and phase coherence at T_c changes nothing local, hence no coherence peak. |\n216\t| **NMR ν ≈ 0.2** | constant (Korringa) above T_c, Hebel–Slichter peak, then e^{−Δ/T} | Weak-coupling BCS: pairs form at T_c and the gap is full and s-wave in each layer. The BCS density of states N_s(E) diverges at the gap edge and produces the peak; fit Δ(0) = 1.98, T_c = 1.11. |\n217\t| **Resistivity ν = ½** | ρ ∝ e^{3.7/T} | Intrinsic semiconductor: carriers are thermally created holon/doublon rungs across E_g (activation E_g/2). Pairs cannot move because every rung is occupied by one, i.e. a Mott insulator of pairs. |\n218\t| **Resistivity ν ≈ 0.3** | rises 9× on cooling, then drops to 0 at 0.36 | Fermionic carriers are gapped by the pseudogap, while the preformed pairs are slow (near pair-Mott localization). Global phase coherence sets in at T_c = 0.36 ≪ T_MF. |\n219\t| **Resistivity ν ≈ 0.2** | metallic, zero below 1.11 | BCS: T_c = T_MF = Δ/1.76. |\n220\t\n221\t---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n222\t\n223\t## 6. Task 4 — predicted ARPES intensity (after division by the Fermi function)\n224\t\n225\t![ARPES](figures/fig4_arpes_predictions.png)\n226\t\n227\tThe intensity divided by the Fermi function is the spectral function A(k, ω) of the top layer. With t⊥ = 0 it is\n228\talso the spectral function of every layer. It is plotted along Γ(0,0) → X(½,0) → M(½,½) → Γ in the window\n229\tω ∈ [−10, 10] relative to μ. This window contains both Hubbard bands at ν = ½ and the full Bogoliubov spectra of\n230\tthe doped crystals. One linear colour scale is shared by the three panels.\n231\t\n232\tWhat can actually be measured: dividing by f(ω) restores the unoccupied side only up to a few k_BT above μ. At\n233\tlow T the occupied branches are directly measurable: the lower Hubbard band at ν = ½, and the v_k²-weighted\n234\tBogoliubov branch with its back-bending at k_F in the superconductors. The upper branches shown above μ are what\n235\tthe divided intensity converges to as the thermal population grows. They are equally fixed by the theory, but\n236\treaching them needs higher T or an inverse-photoemission or pump–probe measurement.\n237\t\n238\t* ν = ½: CPT of the model on a 16-site (4×2×2, orientation-averaged) bilayer cluster at (U, J⊥) = (1.8, 6.5) (§8).\n239\t* ν ≈ 0.3 and 0.2: the coherent superconducting state in Bogoliubov form,\n240\t  A = u_k² δ(ω − E_k) + v_k² δ(ω + E_k), E_k = (ξ_k² + Δ_k²)^{1/2}, ξ_k = ε_k − μ₀(ν), with Lorentzian width\n241\t  0.06. μ is held at the normal-state value μ₀(ν) found in the STS fit of (c), so the underlying Fermi surface\n242\t  encloses ν.\n243\t  * ν ≈ 0.2: Δ = 2.03, the J⊥ = 6.6 mean-field value (STS: 1.96).\n244\t  * ν ≈ 0.3: two-scale gap Δ(ξ) = Δ_∞ − (Δ_∞ − Δ₀)e^{−|ξ|/w}, with Δ₀ = 2.85 (coherent gap at k_F), Δ_∞ = 5.23\n245\t    (local rung-pair scale, cf. the half-filled spin gap) and w = 1.08. The magnitudes are fixed by STS (b);\n246\t    the J⊥ mean field alone gives Δ = 2.44 and misses Δ_∞.\n247\t  * Strong-coupling cross-check: CPT on 16-site doped bilayer clusters gives half-gaps 1.6 (ν = 0.19) and 2.1\n248\t    (ν = 0.31). The lower band peaks at M (−4); the upper band bottoms at Γ (+4); indirect gap 7.9. | An insulator whose gap is not set at a Fermi surface. The gap is local (rung-singlet binding), not a nesting or pairing gap. |\n256\t| ν = ½ | Each band is a copy of the bare band at half width (ε_k/2), and the two copies are *translated*, not mirrored. | Strong correlation: carriers move through singlets with amplitude t/2. No particle–hole (Bogoliubov) mixing, so no condensate. |\n257\t| ν = ½ | No replica (shadow) bands folded by (½,½). | No doubled cell. Confirms no CDW or antiferromagnetism, consistent with diffraction and NMR. |\n258\t| ν = ½ | No bonding–antibonding splitting. | t⊥ ≈ 0: the interlayer coupling is pure exchange, not hopping. |\n259\t| ν = ½ | Weight moves from the lower band (near Γ) to the upper band (near M). | Weights ½ ∓ ε_k/(2E_ex). The three panels are one crossover tuned by filling. |\n264\t\n265\t---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n266\t\n267\t## 7. Task 5 — Green's-function zeros at ν = ½ and the Luttinger count\n268\t\n269\t![zeros](figures/fig5_zeros.png)\n270\t\n271\t**Procedure.**\n272\t\n273\t1. Take the predicted A(k, ω) at ν = ½ (CPT) on a 48×48 k-grid and an ω-grid with step 0.005 over [−16, 16]\n274\t   (width 0.02).\n275\t2. Measure ω from the T → 0 chemical potential at midgap (the band edges are determined from the spectrum\n276\t   itself).\n277\t3. Reconstruct the real part by Kramers–Kronig: Re G(k, 0) = −P∫dω′ A(k, ω′)/ω′. Since A vanishes in the gap\n278\t   this is regular.\n279\t4. The spectral sum rule is 0.9988, the rest lying in tails outside the window.\n280\t5. The KK result agrees with G(k, 0) evaluated directly from the same Green's function. The zero contour is\n281\t   then traced on a 241×241 grid.\n282\t\n283\t**Result.** Re G(k, 0) > 0 over most of the zone, i.e. the lower band dominates. It changes sign on a **small\n284\tclosed curve around M = (½, ½)**.\n285\t\n286\t| Cluster used for the prediction | fraction of BZ on the Γ side of the zero curve |\n287\t|---|---|\n288\t| 8-site bilayer (2×2×2) | 0.914 |\n289\t| 12-site bilayer (3×2×2, orientation-averaged) | 0.871 |\n290\t| 16-site bilayer (4×2×2, orientation-averaged) | **0.855** (KK on 48² grid: 0.856) |\n291\t| control, t′ = 0, 8-site | 0.504 (= ½ within grid resolution) |\n292\t| parameter sensitivity, 12-site: (U, J⊥) = (1.0, 7.1) / (2.2, 6.1) | 0.870 / 0.861 |\n293\t| parameter sensitivity, 12-site: t′ = 0.18 / 0.22 | 0.848 / 0.895 |\n294\t\n295\t**Independent check without CPT.** The exact Green's function of the periodic 16-site bilayer cluster (ED), at\n296\tits own midgap, gives G(K, 0) = +0.027 (Γ), +0.009 (X), +0.009 ((¼,¼)) and **−0.013 (M)**. Its band weights also\n297\tfollow the strong-coupling form ½ ∓ ε_K/(2E_ex), with hole weights 0.725, 0.465, 0.502 and 0.337. The sign\n298\tstructure, positive on the Γ side and negative at M, is exactly that of the CPT zero surface (Fig. 5(c),\n299\tdiamonds). The larger |G(M)| in the exact cluster suggests the M-pocket is, if anything, somewhat larger than in\n300\tthe 12-site CPT.\n301\t\n302\t**Comparison with ν.** The fraction, **0.85 ± 0.03**, is far from ν = 0.5. The quoted value is the 16-site result, extrapolated using the converging cluster sequence (≈ 0.85). The uncertainty combines the cluster-size trend (±0.01), t′ = 0.20 ± 0.02 (±0.024) and (U, J⊥) (±0.01). Luttinger's theorem in its\n303\tGreen's-function form (Σ_k θ[G(k,0)] = ν) fails for this insulator.\n304\t\n305\t*Why.* To first order in t/E_ex the model gives G(k, ω) ∝ (ω − ω_z)/[(ω − E₊(k))(ω − E₋(k))]. Its zero ω_z\n306\tis k-independent and sits at the centre of the atomic levels. The midgap chemical potential is displaced from it\n307\tby half the band-centre offset, −ε_c/2 = 2t′ = 0.4, because t′ makes the bare band asymmetric (ε_max + ε_min =\n308\t−8t′). At ω = μ, G therefore has the same sign almost everywhere. Only the k-dependent (inter-site) part of the\n309\tself-energy, which CPT captures, bends the zero surface down through μ near M, where the upper band is heaviest.\n310\tWith t′ = 0, particle–hole symmetry pins the zero surface to ε_k = 0, enclosing exactly ½ (confirmed\n311\tnumerically). The count depends on where μ sits in the gap, as noted by Rosch (2007) and Dave–Phillips–Kane\n312\t(2013). So the Luttinger volume of zeros is not protected in a Mott insulator without particle–hole symmetry, in\n313\tcontrast to the doped superconductors, whose minimum-gap (underlying) Fermi surface encloses ν.\n314\t\n315\t**The zero band** (Fig. 5(d)). Scanning the reference energy through the gap shows where the zeros live. They\n316\tform a narrow, weakly dispersing band ω_z(k), running from ≈ −0.15 (at M) to ≈ +0.65 (at Γ) relative to the\n317\tmidgap. As ω_ref crosses this band, the fraction of the zone with G > 0 sweeps from 1 to 0. The value ν = ½ would\n318\tbe obtained only if the chemical potential sat ≈ 0.25 above midgap, i.e. at the centre of the zero band. In the\n319\tT → 0 limit μ sits at the midgap instead, by the law of mass action for the thermally excited holons and doublons.\n320\tThat point cuts the zero band only near M, giving 0.855 (16-site cluster; 0.871 for 12 sites). The deviation from ν therefore measures\n321\tthe mismatch between μ and the zero band. That mismatch is set by t′ (≈ 2t′ at first order, reduced by the\n322\tdispersion of ω_z(k)).\n323\t\n324\t---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n325\t\n326\t## 8. Methods, approximations and system sizes\n327\t\n328\t* **Exact diagonalization (ED).** A matrix-free Lanczos code was written for this problem (numba, Kronecker-sum\n329\t  H·v, rung spin-flip terms; `analysis/ed_hubbard.py`, `ed_bilayer.py`). It was verified against free fermions,\n330\t  the two-site Hubbard model, and rung-singlet product states.\n331\t  * Single-layer attractive Hubbard model: periodic clusters of 10 (√10×√10), 16 (4×4) and 20 (√20×√20) sites.\n332\t  * Bilayer model: periodic 16-site cluster (8 rungs, √8×√8), Hilbert-space dimension up to 1.66×10⁸.\n333\t  * Quantities: gaps (E(N+1)+E(N−1)−2E(N))/2, spin gaps E(S_z=1)−E(S_z=0), and phase stiffness from twisted\n334\t    boundary conditions.\n335\t* **Cluster perturbation theory (CPT).** Open bilayer clusters of 8 (2×2×2), 12 (3×2×2) and 16 (4×2×2) sites.\n336\t  The cluster Green's function comes from a band (block) Lanczos method, checked against an exact Lehmann sum\n337\t  to 10⁻¹³. It is coupled through the in-plane inter-cluster hopping and periodized\n338\t  (`analysis/cpt_bilayer.py`, `cpt_analyze.py`). Non-square clusters are orientation-averaged. CPT is exact at\n339\t  U = J⊥ = 0, which was checked. The 16-site half-filled cluster (Hilbert space 1.66×10⁸) exceeds the 32 GiB memory of the workstation\n340\t  container with an 8-vector block. It was therefore split with the mirror y → 1−y into even/odd 4×4 blocks\n341\t  (`analysis/cpt_half16_lean.py`), which reproduces the full block Lanczos to 10⁻⁷ on the 8-site cluster. Doped\n342\t  CPT: 16-site clusters with 6 and 10 electrons (ν = 0.1875, 0.3125).\n343\t* **Exact cluster Green's function.** G(K, ω) of the periodic 16-site bilayer at its allowed momenta (Γ, X, M,\n344\t  (½,½)/2) by Lanczos continued fractions (`analysis/ed_bilayer_gk.py`). This is a CPT-independent check of the\n345\t  sign structure of G at midgap.\n346\t* **Mean field.** BCS for interlayer singlet pairing driven by J⊥ (`analysis/bcs_bilayer.py`), with a 256×256\n347\t  k-grid and density fixed by the number equation.\n348\t* **Two-body problem.** Exact pair binding energy of the attractive model on the infinite lattice (1024² k-grid).\n349\t* **Data fits.** Weighted least squares. The quoted errors are from the covariance, rescaled by χ²/dof when\n350\t  > 1. The NMR error bars in the file are conservative (χ²/dof ≈ 0.15 for good fits).\n351\t\n352\t---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n353\t\n354\t## 9. Limitations\n355\t\n356\t* A bilayer block is *inferred* (from LSM plus the data), not stated in the problem. It is the most economical\n357\t  structure that allows the observed featureless gapped state with the observed (large) spin gap.\n358\t* A large J⊥ with t⊥ ≈ 0 requires the interlayer exchange to be transmitted by other orbitals (apical O,\n359\t  d_{z²}-like admixture), not by hopping within the active band.\n360\t* The transition temperatures of the doped crystals are mean-field-like (T_c(0.2) = T_MF). A strictly 2D model\n361\t  would give T_KT ≲ 0.3 at ν = 0.2. The measured T_c therefore implies three-dimensional coupling between\n362\t  bilayers, which the in-plane model does not describe. The T_c dome between the measured points is schematic.\n363\t* At the representative parameters the model's spin gap (4.7) is about 15% below the NMR value (5.5 ± 0.5). Raising\n364\t  J⊥ to fit it would overshoot the doped gaps by a similar amount. Finite clusters also overestimate the doped\n365\t  gaps (ED: 2.45 vs 1.96 at ν ≈ 0.2). The finite-cluster CPT of the doped crystals does not resolve the\n366\t  high-energy two-scale structure of STS (b), which is therefore taken from the data (§6).\n367\t* The size of the M-pocket of zeros (Task 5) depends on the k-dependent self-energy and moves somewhat with\n368\t  cluster size (0.914 → 0.871 → 0.855 for 8, 12, 16 sites, converging). The qualitative result (Γ side ≫ ν, a small closed curve\n369\t  around M, exactly ½ when t′ = 0) is robust.\n370\t\n371\t---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n372\t\n373\t## 10. Answers in brief\n\n| Task | Answer |\n|---|---|\n| **State at ν = 1/2** | A **featureless, interaction-driven insulator of interlayer spin singlets** (a \"rung-singlet\" Mott insulator). Every vertical TM–TM pair of a perovskite **bilayer** block holds one spin singlet. Nothing is broken: no charge order, no magnetic order, no superconductivity, no doubled cell, no topological order, and the ground state is unique. Spin gap Δ_s ≈ 5.5 from NMR (the rung singlet→triplet gap; model: 4.7–5.0). Single-particle gap E_g = 7.9. Transport gap E_g/2 ≈ 3.7–4.0. |\n| **1. Effective theory** | A one-orbital **bilayer Hubbard–Heisenberg model** on the bilayer square lattice, with one rung (2 TM sites) per primitive cell: H = −t Σ c†c (nn, in plane) − t′ Σ c†c (nnn, in plane) − t⊥ Σ c†c (rung) + U Σ n↑n↓ + J⊥ Σ (S₁·S₂ − n₁n₂/4) − μN. Values: **t = 1.00 ± 0.02**, **t′ = +0.20 ± 0.02**, **\\|t⊥\\| < 0.2**, **U = 1.4 ± 0.8**, **J⊥ = 6.6 ± 0.5**. It conserves charge (separately per layer when t⊥ = 0), SU(2) spin, time reversal, translations and D4h. It lacks particle–hole symmetry (t′), the η-pseudospin SU(2), and any Lieb–Schultz–Mattis obstruction (two electrons per cell at ν = 1/2). |\n| **2. Phase diagram** | Band insulators at ν = 0, 1. Interlayer s± superconducting domes on both sides of ν = 1/2, with T_c bounded by the mean-field pairing scale T_MF(ν) and driven to zero at ν = 1/2. There the rung pairs fill every rung and localize, giving the rung-singlet insulator. A preformed-pair (pseudogap) regime lies between T_c and T*, and a normal metal above. Low → high T: **ν = 1/2**: rung-singlet insulator → (T ≳ 5) correlated paramagnet / bad metal. **ν ≈ 0.3**: s± superconductor (T < 0.36) → preformed rung pairs, pseudogap, insulating-like (0.36 < T < 2.5–3) → normal metal. **ν ≈ 0.2**: BCS-like s± superconductor (T < 1.11) → normal Fermi-liquid metal. |\n| **3. Data explained** | See the table in §5: every feature maps onto one ingredient of the model. |\n| **4. ARPES** | **ν = 1/2:** two rigidly translated, half-width bands (ε_k/2 ± E_ex/2); indirect gap from M (top of the lower band, −4) to Γ (bottom of the upper band, +4); no replica bands. **ν ≈ 0.3:** Bogoliubov back-bending at k_F with Δ ≈ 2.9, plus a second, local pairing scale ≈ 5.2 away from k_F. **ν ≈ 0.2:** sharp BCS Bogoliubov bands with Δ ≈ 2.0 on the bare band. |\n| **5. Zeros of G at ω = 0, ν = 1/2** | A small **closed curve around M = (½,½)**. The side containing Γ covers **0.85 ± 0.03 of the Brillouin zone** (16-site CPT: 0.855; 8 → 12 → 16 sites: 0.914 → 0.871 → 0.855), compared with ν = 0.5, so Luttinger's theorem written with zeros fails. The cause is particle–hole asymmetry (t′ ≠ 0): the zeros form a narrow band centred about 0.25 above the midgap chemical potential (2t′ at first order), so μ cuts it only near M. Control calculation: with t′ = 0 the same method gives exactly 0.50. |\n\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## 1. What the measurements say before any model is chosen\n\n### 1.1 Band structure (STS, Fig. 1(d), high T)\n\nA least-squares fit of panel (d) to the density of states of\nε_k = −2t(cos k_x + cos k_y) − 4t′ cos k_x cos k_y, with filling ν, a Gaussian resolution and a smooth\nbackground, gives:\n\n* **t = 1.000 ± 0.004 (stat.) ± 0.02 (syst.)**, i.e. D is the nearest-neighbour hopping\n* **t′ = 0.195 ± 0.002 (stat.) ± 0.02 (syst.)**\n* **ν = 0.300 ± 0.001**\n\nThe band edges (−4.0, +4.2 relative to μ) and the van Hove peak at +1.75 are reproduced to within 0.05. t′ > 0 in\nthis sign convention puts the van Hove singularity above the band centre and the band bottom at Γ. There\nis no second van Hove peak, which bounds a bonding–antibonding splitting at 2|t⊥| ≲ 0.3.\n\n### 1.2 The half-filled crystal\n\n1. **Hubbard-like split bands.** The two bands in Fig. 1(a) are *rigid translates* of each other. Their\n   overlap after a shift of 12.1 ± 0.1 is 0.976; the overlap of the mirror image is only 0.70. Each band is\n   4.0 wide, i.e. half the bare bandwidth 8t. A superconducting gap would make the spectrum mirror-symmetric\n   about μ (Bogoliubov poles at ±E_k), so this is **not** a pairing gap of a condensate.\n2. **Spectral weights.** The weight below the gap is 0.50 (= ν). The lower band is weighted toward its bottom\n   (states near Γ) and the upper band toward its top (states near M). The ratio follows\n   Z∓ = ½ ∓ ε_k/(2E_ex) with E_ex ≈ 12, the strong-coupling (Hubbard-I-type) form.\n3. **Gaps.** The single-particle gap is E_g = 7.9 ± 0.1 (edges at ±3.95). The resistivity is activated with\n   Δ_ρ = 3.72 ± 0.05 ≈ E_g/2, as for an intrinsic semiconductor with μ at midgap.\n4. **Spin gap.** 1/(T₁T) falls by five decades between T = 4.4 and 0.45. It is a pure exponential with\n   Δ_s = 5.5 ± 0.5 (a free power-law prefactor T^p fits to p = −0.04 ± 0.38). The STS density of states alone\n   would give an activation of only 3.75 (Korringa estimate from Fig. 1(a)). **Spin excitations therefore cost\n   more than the thermal charge carriers**: Δ_s = 5.5 > Δ_ρ = 3.7, with Δ_s < E_g = 7.9.\n5. **No broken symmetry.** There are no new or split diffraction peaks, all TM sites are equivalent, the TM NMR\n   line is single, and STS is the same everywhere.\n\n**Lieb–Schultz–Mattis (LSM) constraint.** At ν = 1/2 each TM carries one electron. If the primitive cell\ncontained one TM, the LSM–Oshikawa–Hastings theorem would forbid a unique, gapped, fully symmetric ground state.\nThe only way out would be topological order, with gaps bounded by the exchange scale (≈ 4t²/U ≈ 0.3), far below\nthe measured 5.5 and 3.7. The data therefore require **an even number of electrons per primitive cell**, i.e. two\ncrystallographically equivalent TM sites per cell. This is exactly what a perovskite **bilayer** block provides\n(two TMO₂ planes sharing apical oxygens, related by a mirror plane). It is compatible with every structural\nstatement: in-plane period a, all TM equivalent, one NMR line.\n\n### 1.3 The doped crystals\n\n* **ν ≈ 0.2.** Panel (c) is BCS on the bare band: **Δ = 1.964 ± 0.002**, with μ equal to the normal-state value\n  μ₀(0.2) = −1.92 (fit −1.922 ± 0.004), so the underlying Fermi surface encloses exactly ν. The NMR shows a\n  Hebel–Slichter peak (1.7× the normal value at T ≈ 0.8–1.0) and is fitted by BCS with Δ(0) = 1.98 and\n  **T_c = 1.11** (2Δ/T_c = 3.6). The resistivity is metallic and vanishes below T_c = 1.11 ± 0.04. Pairing is\n  s-wave-like (full gap, coherence peak) and weak-coupling.\n* **ν ≈ 0.3.** There is a hard gap, but no single BCS gap fits (rms 0.16). Panel (b) needs an energy-dependent\n  gap: **Δ₀ = 2.85 ± 0.02** at the Fermi surface, rising to **Δ_∞ = 5.23** for |ξ_k| ≳ 1 (rms 0.034). That\n  second scale matches the half-filled spin gap. The NMR gap is 2.7 ± 0.1 both above and below\n  **T_c = 0.36 ± 0.04** and opens at T* ≈ 2.5–3. The normal state is insulating-like (ρ ∝ e^{0.9/T}).\n  This is a strongly paired superconductor with preformed pairs, where T_c ≪ Δ.\n* **Trend toward ν = 1/2.** The gap grows (1.96 → 2.85 → 3.95), T_c falls (1.11 → 0.36 → 0) and coherence is\n  lost. This is the doping evolution of a Mott insulator, here one of *pairs*.\n\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## 2. Why the standard single-layer models fail (and the bilayer does not)\n\n| Candidate | Fatal problem (quantified) |\n|---|---|\n| Repulsive one-layer Hubbard, U ≈ 12 | Local moments with J = 4t²/U ≈ 0.33: 1/T₁ would be roughly constant (1/T₁T rising) for T ≫ J, against the observed five-decade activated drop. A spin gap of 5.5 ≫ J is impossible. It also gives d-wave nodal pairing, not a full gap with a Hebel–Slichter peak. |\n| Attractive one-layer Hubbard, U ≈ −12 (fixes Fig. 1(a) and Δ_s ≈ \\|U\\|/2) | (i) **Exact diagonalization** (10, 16, 20-site clusters) gives single-particle gaps of 3.4–3.6 at ν ≈ 0.2 and 3.7–4.0 at ν ≈ 0.3, versus 1.96 and 2.85 measured. The gap decreases toward the two-body value E_b/2 = 2.06 only as ν → 0 (2.5–2.6 for a single pair on 16–20 sites). (ii) Spin and charge excitations are the same quasiparticles, so it cannot give Δ_s > Δ_ρ. (iii) Pairs hop with J ≈ 4t²/\\|U\\| ≈ 0.33 and would conduct for T ≫ J, so ρ(0.45)/ρ(4) ≈ 1, not 1600. (iv) At fixed U, lower density is *more* BEC-like, the opposite of the trend. (v) The high-T spectrum at ν = 0.3 would carry Hubbard satellites holding 30% of the weight; they are absent in Fig. 1(d). |\n| One layer, topological spin liquid | Allowed by LSM, but its gaps are bounded by ~J ≈ 0.3, not 5.5. |\n| **Bilayer, strong interlayer singlet coupling J⊥, small U, t⊥ ≈ 0** | Explains every item quantitatively (§5). It is LSM-allowed: two electrons per primitive cell at ν = 1/2. |\n\n![model selection](figures/fig6_model_selection.png)\n\n*Fig. 6.* (a) Single-particle half-gap versus filling. The attractive single-layer model (ED on 10, 16 and 20\nsites) stays near 3.4–4.2 at every filling. The bilayer model gives 2.45, 2.70 and 4.10 at ν = 0.19, 0.31, 0.5\n(ED), and its J⊥ mean field gives 1.98 at ν = 0.2. Measured: 1.96, 2.6–2.85, 3.95. (b) At ν = ½ only the bilayer\nreproduces the ordering *spin gap > thermal charge gap* seen in NMR versus resistivity.\n\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## 3. Task 1 — the effective theory\n\n**Degrees of freedom.** Spin-½ electrons in the single active orbital of each TM. This is a d_{x²−y²}-like\norbital σ-bonded to the in-plane oxygens. Its O admixture is what makes the hopping range reach t′, and its\napical-O / d_{z²} admixture is what transmits the interlayer exchange. Each site has four states: empty, ↑, ↓\nand doubly occupied.\n\n**Lattice and unit cell.** The bilayer square lattice. A site is labelled (i, l): i runs over an in-plane square\nlattice with constant a, and l = 1, 2 labels the two planes of one perovskite block. The primitive cell is one\n**rung**, i.e. the two TM sites stacked along c, related by the mirror plane between the layers. The Brillouin\nzone is the in-plane square zone. ν = 1/2 means two electrons per primitive cell.\n\n**Hamiltonian** (every term):\n\n```\nH = − t   Σ_{⟨ij⟩, l, σ}  ( c†_{ilσ} c_{jlσ} + h.c. )          in-plane nearest-neighbour hopping\n    − t′  Σ_{⟨⟨ij⟩⟩, l, σ} ( c†_{ilσ} c_{jlσ} + h.c. )          in-plane next-nearest-neighbour hopping\n    − t⊥  Σ_{i, σ}         ( c†_{i1σ} c_{i2σ} + h.c. )          interlayer (rung) hopping\n    + U   Σ_{i, l}          n_{il↑} n_{il↓}                     on-site Coulomb repulsion\n    + J⊥  Σ_i              ( S_{i1}·S_{i2} − ¼ n_{i1} n_{i2} )  interlayer (rung) singlet exchange\n    − μ   Σ_{i, l}          n_{il}                              chemical potential (sets ν)\n```\n\nso that ε_k = −2t(cos k_x + cos k_y) − 4t′ cos k_x cos k_y (k in units of 1/a) within each layer.\n\n**Coefficients and how they were determined.**\n\n| Coefficient | Value | Uncertainty | Determined from |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| t | 1.00 | ± 0.02 | fit of the high-T STS (d): band edges and van Hove peak; consistent with (a) and (c) |\n| t′ | +0.20 | ± 0.02 | same fit (van Hove peak 1.75 above μ, asymmetric band edges); χ² profile minimum at 0.20 |\n| t⊥ | 0 | \\|t⊥\\| < 0.2 | no bonding–antibonding splitting of the van Hove peak in (d), resolution 0.14 |\n| J⊥ | 6.6 | ± 0.5 | (i) half-filled NMR spin gap 5.5 ± 0.5 = triplon gap ≈ J⊥ − (1.4 to 1.8) (ED, 16-site bilayer) → J⊥ = 7.1 ± 0.6; (ii) BCS gap at ν ≈ 0.2: Δ = 1.96 requires J⊥ = 6.5 in mean field; (iii) T_c(0.2) = 1.11 = T_MF requires J⊥ = 6.45; (iv) ED doped gaps prefer 5.5–6.5. Weighted combination. |\n| U | 1.4 | ± 0.8 | half-filled single-particle gap: E_g/2 = 3.95 = U/2 + 3J⊥/4 − (1.69 ± 0.03), the last term from band broadening (ED); uncertainty dominated by J⊥. The splitting between Hubbard-band centres, 12.1 ≈ U + 3J⊥/2 + O(t²), and the bare band at ν ≤ 0.3 (Fig. 1(c,d)), which requires U ≲ W/2, are consistent. |\n| μ | sets ν | — | μ(ν) |\n\nExact diagonalization of the final parameter set (U = 1.8, J⊥ = 6.5) on the 16-site bilayer gives\na single-particle half-gap of **4.10** (data 3.95) and a spin gap of **4.72** (data 5.5 ± 0.5). The pair stiffness from twisted boundary conditions is D = 1.06 per rung at ν = 0.19, 0.74 at ν = 0.31 and 0.02 at ν = ½, i.e. 75%, 42% and 1% of the free-electron value. The other runs give (half-gap / spin gap): (U, J⊥) = (3.85, 5.5): 4.33 / 4.13; (3.0, 5.5): 3.96 / 3.97; (1.4, 6.9): 4.18 / 5.02. At fixed charge gap the spin gap rises with J⊥ and reaches the NMR value 5.5 at J⊥ ≈ 7.5, where the doped gaps and T_c(0.2) would come out ≈ 15% too high. J⊥ = 6.6 ± 0.5 balances these constraints.\n\n*Stability of the half-filled state.* The in-plane superexchange through the rung-singlet background is\nJ_∥ ≈ 4t²/E_ex ≈ 0.35, so J⊥/J_∥ ≈ 19. That lies far inside the rung-singlet (quantum-disordered) phase of the\nbilayer Heisenberg model, whose critical ratio is 2.52, so no in-plane antiferromagnetism develops. A\ncharge-density wave would have to break rung singlets (cost ≈ J⊥ per rung), so none develops either. At exactly\nν = ½ every rung holds one pair, which cannot move without creating an empty and a doubly occupied rung (cost\n2U + J⊥ in the atomic limit), so there is no superconductivity.\n\n**Symmetries the model has**\n\n* U(1) charge. For t⊥ = 0 the charge of *each layer* is separately conserved, an extra U(1).\n* SU(2) spin rotation (no spin–orbit term).\n* Time reversal.\n* Translations of the square lattice (one rung per cell).\n* The full point group D4h of a perovskite bilayer: C₄ about c, vertical mirrors, the horizontal mirror σ_h\n  exchanging the layers, and inversion through the rung centre.\n\n**Symmetries the model lacks**\n\n* **Particle–hole symmetry.** t′ ≠ 0, while the U and J⊥ terms are particle–hole symmetric only up to a shift\n  of μ. Consequences: the van Hove peak lies above mid-band; the half-filled spectrum is not mirror-symmetric\n  about its centre; the Green's-function zero is not pinned to μ (Task 5); and the phase diagram is asymmetric\n  about ν = ½.\n* **η-pseudospin (charge) SU(2)**, broken by t′ and by the density part of the J⊥ term. Charge order and pairing are not degenerate.\n* **An LSM obstruction.** Two electrons per cell at ν = ½ permit a unique gapped symmetric ground state. This is\n  why the half-filled insulator can be featureless *without* topological order.\n* **Interlayer band coherence.** t⊥ ≈ 0, so there is no bonding–antibonding splitting.\n* No spin–orbit coupling, no disorder, and no term that doubles the cell.\n\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## 4. Task 2 — phase diagram\n\n![phase diagram](figures/fig3_phase_diagram.png)\n\n**How it was obtained** (approximations stated):\n\n* **T_MF(ν):** BCS mean-field onset of interlayer singlet pairing driven by J⊥ (gap equation\n  1 = J⊥ N⁻¹Σ_k tanh(E_k/2T)/2E_k at fixed ν, 256×256 k-grid). It is a broad dome peaking at ν ≈ 0.5–0.55,\n  near the van Hove filling, and is an *upper bound* for T_c.\n* **Rung-singlet regime near ν = ½:** the local singlet–triplet splitting (ED spin gap ≈ 5) sets a\n  crossover T_s ≈ Δ_s/ln 3 ≈ 5 below which every rung is a singlet. At exactly ν = ½ the pairs fill all rungs,\n  their motion is blocked, the pair stiffness collapses (ED, twisted boundaries: its coherent fraction D/D_free falls from 0.75 at ν = 0.19 to 0.42 at ν = 0.31 and to 0.013 at ν = ½, where D = 0.02 per rung), and the state\n  is the rung-singlet insulator.\n* **T_c(ν):** T_c = T_MF(ν) · min[1, (Z(ν)/Z(0.2))^p], with Z = D/D_free the coherent fraction of the pair\n  stiffness from ED (0.75 at ν = 0.19, 0.42 at ν = 0.31, 0.013 at ν = ½). The single exponent\n  p = 2.8 is fixed by the measured T_c(0.3) = 0.36; T_c(0.2) = T_MF = 1.13 then follows. This is an\n  interpolation, not a calculation of T_c. A strictly 2D model would cap T_c at T_KT ≲ 0.3; the measured,\n  mean-field-like T_c implies coupling between bilayers. T_c → 0 for ν → 0 (dilute BCS) and ν → ½ (Mott\n  localization of rung pairs). The ν > ½ side follows from the particle–hole transform (ν → 1−ν, t′ → −t′),\n  which T_MF includes; Z is mirrored.\n* The crossover line T* and the precise dome shape between the measured points are **schematic**. The\n  computed objects are T_MF, the rung-singlet scale, and the vanishing stiffness at ν = ½.\n\n**Phases of each crystal, from low to high temperature**\n\n| Crystal | Phases |\n|---|---|\n| ν = 1/2 | rung-singlet insulator (no broken symmetry; gaps Δ_s ≈ 5.5, E_g ≈ 7.9) up to T_s ≈ 5 → crossover to a correlated paramagnetic bad metal / semiconductor |\n| ν ≈ 0.3 | interlayer s± superconductor (T < 0.36) → preformed rung pairs: pseudogap, spin gap 2.7, insulating-like ρ (0.36 < T < T* ≈ 2.5–3) → normal metal (T ≳ 3) |\n| ν ≈ 0.2 | interlayer s± superconductor, BCS-like (T < 1.11) → normal Fermi-liquid metal (T > 1.11; T* = T_c) |\n\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## 5. Task 3 — how the theory produces each set of measurements\n\n![STS vs theory](figures/fig1_sts_vs_theory.png)\n![NMR and resistivity](figures/fig2_nmr_rho_fits.png)\n\n| Measurement | Observation | Feature of the theory that produces it |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Diffraction** | period a, all TM equivalent, no new or split peaks down to the lowest T | The ν = ½ ground state is a product of rung singlets (dressed by virtual hopping). It is unique and invariant under all lattice symmetries, so no superlattice is needed. With two TM per cell the gap needs no symmetry breaking (LSM satisfied). Pairs on the doped side are interlayer, uniform and s-wave. |\n| **NMR line** | single TM line | Both TM of a rung are equivalent by σ_h. There are no ordered moments (singlets) and no charge disproportionation. |\n| **STS (a), ν = ½** | hard gap 7.9; two bands 4.0 wide, rigidly shifted by 12.1; weight 0.50 below | Removing an electron leaves a singly occupied rung (cost ≈ J⊥). Adding one makes a three-electron rung (cost ≈ U + J⊥/2). Both excitations hop through the singlet background with amplitude t/2 (the overlap of a moved electron with a rung singlet). This gives E_±(k) ≈ ±E_ex/2 + ε_k/2, bands of width W/2 and weights ½ ∓ ε_k/(2E_ex). Here E_ex = U + 3J⊥/2 ≈ 11.3, plus ≈ 0.6 of second-order level repulsion, which reproduces the measured splitting 12.1. The gap is E_ex − 3.4 ≈ 7.9 (ED on 16 sites: 8.2). CPT reproduces positions and edges (Fig. 1(a)). |\n| **STS (b), ν ≈ 0.3** | gap 2.6–2.85 at E_F; peaks at ±5.1, edges at ±6.5 | Doping makes rung pairs mobile and they condense. Near k_F the coherent Bogoliubov gap is Δ₀ ≈ 2.85 (mean field: 2.4–2.65). Far from k_F the states still feel the *local* rung-singlet binding ≈ 5.2. The result is a two-scale gap Δ(ξ). |\n| **STS (c), ν ≈ 0.2** | BCS: Δ = 1.96, coherence peaks, bare band | Weak-coupling interlayer s± BCS state on the bare band: Δ = 1.98 for J⊥ = 6.5, with the underlying Fermi surface enclosing ν. U is small, so the band is unrenormalized. |\n| **STS (d), ν ≈ 0.3, high T** | bare t-t′ band, ν = 0.30 | Above all pairing scales the model is a weakly correlated metal (U ≲ W/2, t⊥ ≈ 0): one band per layer, no Hubbard satellites. |\n| **NMR ν = ½** | activated, Δ_s = 5.5 | The rung singlet → triplet gap J⊥ − (triplon dispersion): 4.7 for (U, J⊥) = (1.8, 6.5), 1.5σ below the measured 5.5 ± 0.5. Thermal triplons relax the nucleus. Spin and charge gaps are distinct objects here (singlet–triplet vs. single-particle), which is why Δ_s ≠ Δ_ρ. |\n| **NMR ν ≈ 0.3** | activated, 2.7, unchanged across T_c, onset at T* ≈ 2.5–3 | Preformed rung pairs. The quasiparticle gap opens at T*, and phase coherence at T_c changes nothing local, hence no coherence peak. |\n| **NMR ν ≈ 0.2** | constant (Korringa) above T_c, Hebel–Slichter peak, then e^{−Δ/T} | Weak-coupling BCS: pairs form at T_c and the gap is full and s-wave in each layer. The BCS density of states N_s(E) diverges at the gap edge and produces the peak; fit Δ(0) = 1.98, T_c = 1.11. |\n| **Resistivity ν = ½** | ρ ∝ e^{3.7/T} | Intrinsic semiconductor: carriers are thermally created holon/doublon rungs across E_g (activation E_g/2). Pairs cannot move because every rung is occupied by one, i.e. a Mott insulator of pairs. |\n| **Resistivity ν ≈ 0.3** | rises 9× on cooling, then drops to 0 at 0.36 | Fermionic carriers are gapped by the pseudogap, while the preformed pairs are slow (near pair-Mott localization). Global phase coherence sets in at T_c = 0.36 ≪ T_MF. |\n| **Resistivity ν ≈ 0.2** | metallic, zero below 1.11 | BCS: T_c = T_MF = Δ/1.76. |\n\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## 6. Task 4 — predicted ARPES intensity (after division by the Fermi function)\n\n![ARPES](figures/fig4_arpes_predictions.png)\n\nThe intensity divided by the Fermi function is the spectral function A(k, ω) of the top layer. With t⊥ = 0 it is\nalso the spectral function of every layer. It is plotted along Γ(0,0) → X(½,0) → M(½,½) → Γ in the window\nω ∈ [−10, 10] relative to μ. This window contains both Hubbard bands at ν = ½ and the full Bogoliubov spectra of\nthe doped crystals. One linear colour scale is shared by the three panels.\n\nWhat can actually be measured: dividing by f(ω) restores the unoccupied side only up to a few k_BT above μ. At\nlow T the occupied branches are directly measurable: the lower Hubbard band at ν = ½, and the v_k²-weighted\nBogoliubov branch with its back-bending at k_F in the superconductors. The upper branches shown above μ are what\nthe divided intensity converges to as the thermal population grows. They are equally fixed by the theory, but\nreaching them needs higher T or an inverse-photoemission or pump–probe measurement.\n\n* ν = ½: CPT of the model on a 16-site (4×2×2, orientation-averaged) bilayer cluster at (U, J⊥) = (1.8, 6.5) (§8).\n* ν ≈ 0.3 and 0.2: the coherent superconducting state in Bogoliubov form,\n  A = u_k² δ(ω − E_k) + v_k² δ(ω + E_k), E_k = (ξ_k² + Δ_k²)^{1/2}, ξ_k = ε_k − μ₀(ν), with Lorentzian width\n  0.06. μ is held at the normal-state value μ₀(ν) found in the STS fit of (c), so the underlying Fermi surface\n  encloses ν.\n  * ν ≈ 0.2: Δ = 2.03, the J⊥ = 6.6 mean-field value (STS: 1.96).\n  * ν ≈ 0.3: two-scale gap Δ(ξ) = Δ_∞ − (Δ_∞ − Δ₀)e^{−|ξ|/w}, with Δ₀ = 2.85 (coherent gap at k_F), Δ_∞ = 5.23\n    (local rung-pair scale, cf. the half-filled spin gap) and w = 1.08. The magnitudes are fixed by STS (b);\n    the J⊥ mean field alone gives Δ = 2.44 and misses Δ_∞.\n  * Strong-coupling cross-check: CPT on 16-site doped bilayer clusters gives half-gaps 1.6 (ν = 0.19) and 2.1\n    (ν = 0.31). Periodic-cluster ED gives 2.4 and 2.7. These bracket the measured 1.96 and 2.6–2.85, but the\n    finite-cluster CPT does not resolve the high-energy structure of (b).\n\n**Features of physical significance**\n\n| Filling | Feature | What it implies |\n|---|---|---|\n| ν = ½ | Full gap at every k. The lower band peaks at M (−4); the upper band bottoms at Γ (+4); indirect gap 7.9. | An insulator whose gap is not set at a Fermi surface. The gap is local (rung-singlet binding), not a nesting or pairing gap. |\n| ν = ½ | Each band is a copy of the bare band at half width (ε_k/2), and the two copies are *translated*, not mirrored. | Strong correlation: carriers move through singlets with amplitude t/2. No particle–hole (Bogoliubov) mixing, so no condensate. |\n| ν = ½ | No replica (shadow) bands folded by (½,½). | No doubled cell. Confirms no CDW or antiferromagnetism, consistent with diffraction and NMR. |\n| ν = ½ | No bonding–antibonding splitting. | t⊥ ≈ 0: the interlayer coupling is pure exchange, not hopping. |\n| ν = ½ | Weight moves from the lower band (near Γ) to the upper band (near M). | Weights ½ ∓ ε_k/(2E_ex). The zeros of G (Luttinger surface, Task 5) sit where the two weighted contributions balance. |\n| ν ≈ 0.3 | Bogoliubov back-bending at the underlying k_F (minimum-gap locus). The gap is nodeless and the same in every direction. | A fully gapped s-wave (interlayer s±) condensate. The minimum-gap locus is the underlying Fermi surface, enclosing ν (Luttinger satisfied in the SC state). |\n| ν ≈ 0.3 | Large gap (≈ 2.9) at k_F and a second scale ≈ 5.2 for states away from k_F (bands pushed out to ±5.1 … ±6.5). | Strong pairing with preformed local (rung) pairs, close to the half-filled pair-Mott insulator; low coherence, hence T_c ≪ Δ. |\n| ν ≈ 0.2 | Sharp Bogoliubov bands, Δ ≈ 2.0, full bare dispersion away from k_F. | Weak-coupling BCS on an essentially unrenormalized band, with T_c = Δ/1.76. |\n| Across ν | From 0.2 to 0.3 to ½ the gap grows (2.0 → 2.9 → 4.0 half-gap), the dispersion away from k_F narrows toward ε_k/2, and back-bending (particle–hole mixing) is replaced by rigidly shifted bands. | The evolution from a BCS superconductor, through a strongly paired condensate, to a Mott insulator of local pairs. The three panels are one crossover tuned by filling. |\n\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## 7. Task 5 — Green's-function zeros at ν = ½ and the Luttinger count\n\n![zeros](figures/fig5_zeros.png)\n\n**Procedure.**\n\n1. Take the predicted A(k, ω) at ν = ½ (CPT) on a 48×48 k-grid and an ω-grid with step 0.005 over [−16, 16]\n   (width 0.02).\n2. Measure ω from the T → 0 chemical potential at midgap (the band edges are determined from the spectrum\n   itself).\n3. Reconstruct the real part by Kramers–Kronig: Re G(k, 0) = −P∫dω′ A(k, ω′)/ω′. Since A vanishes in the gap\n   this is regular.\n4. The spectral sum rule is 0.9988, the rest lying in tails outside the window.\n5. The KK result agrees with G(k, 0) evaluated directly from the same Green's function. The zero contour is\n   then traced on a 241×241 grid.\n\n**Result.** Re G(k, 0) > 0 over most of the zone, i.e. the lower band dominates. It changes sign on a **small\nclosed curve around M = (½, ½)**.\n\n| Cluster used for the prediction | fraction of BZ on the Γ side of the zero curve |\n|---|---|\n| 8-site bilayer (2×2×2) | 0.914 |\n| 12-site bilayer (3×2×2, orientation-averaged) | 0.871 |\n| 16-site bilayer (4×2×2, orientation-averaged) | **0.855** (KK on 48² grid: 0.856) |\n| control, t′ = 0, 8-site | 0.504 (= ½ within grid resolution) |\n| parameter sensitivity, 12-site: (U, J⊥) = (1.0, 7.1) / (2.2, 6.1) | 0.870 / 0.861 |\n| parameter sensitivity, 12-site: t′ = 0.18 / 0.22 | 0.848 / 0.895 |\n\n**Independent check without CPT.** The exact Green's function of the periodic 16-site bilayer cluster (ED), at\nits own midgap, gives G(K, 0) = +0.027 (Γ), +0.009 (X), +0.009 ((¼,¼)) and **−0.013 (M)**. Its band weights also\nfollow the strong-coupling form ½ ∓ ε_K/(2E_ex), with hole weights 0.725, 0.465, 0.502 and 0.337. The sign\nstructure, positive on the Γ side and negative at M, is exactly that of the CPT zero surface (Fig. 5(c),\ndiamonds). The larger |G(M)| in the exact cluster suggests the M-pocket is, if anything, somewhat larger than in\nthe 12-site CPT.\n\n**Comparison with ν.** The fraction, **0.85 ± 0.03**, is far from ν = 0.5. The quoted value is the 16-site result, extrapolated using the converging cluster sequence (≈ 0.85). The uncertainty combines the cluster-size trend (±0.01), t′ = 0.20 ± 0.02 (±0.024) and (U, J⊥) (±0.01). Luttinger's theorem in its\nGreen's-function form (Σ_k θ[G(k,0)] = ν) fails for this insulator.\n\n*Why.* To first order in t/E_ex the model gives G(k, ω) ∝ (ω − ω_z)/[(ω − E₊(k))(ω − E₋(k))]. Its zero ω_z\nis k-independent and sits at the centre of the atomic levels. The midgap chemical potential is displaced from it\nby half the band-centre offset, −ε_c/2 = 2t′ = 0.4, because t′ makes the bare band asymmetric (ε_max + ε_min =\n−8t′). At ω = μ, G therefore has the same sign almost everywhere. Only the k-dependent (inter-site) part of the\nself-energy, which CPT captures, bends the zero surface down through μ near M, where the upper band is heaviest.\nWith t′ = 0, particle–hole symmetry pins the zero surface to ε_k = 0, enclosing exactly ½ (confirmed\nnumerically). The count depends on where μ sits in the gap, as noted by Rosch (2007) and Dave–Phillips–Kane\n(2013). So the Luttinger volume of zeros is not protected in a Mott insulator without particle–hole symmetry, in\ncontrast to the doped superconductors, whose minimum-gap (underlying) Fermi surface encloses ν.\n\n**The zero band** (Fig. 5(d)). Scanning the reference energy through the gap shows where the zeros live. They\nform a narrow, weakly dispersing band ω_z(k), running from ≈ −0.15 (at M) to ≈ +0.65 (at Γ) relative to the\nmidgap. As ω_ref crosses this band, the fraction of the zone with G > 0 sweeps from 1 to 0. The value ν = ½ would\nbe obtained only if the chemical potential sat ≈ 0.25 above midgap, i.e. at the centre of the zero band. In the\nT → 0 limit μ sits at the midgap instead, by the law of mass action for the thermally excited holons and doublons.\nThat point cuts the zero band only near M, giving 0.855 (16-site cluster; 0.871 for 12 sites). The deviation from ν therefore measures\nthe mismatch between μ and the zero band. That mismatch is set by t′ (≈ 2t′ at first order, reduced by the\ndispersion of ω_z(k)).\n\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## 8. Methods, approximations and system sizes\n\n* **Exact diagonalization (ED).** A matrix-free Lanczos code was written for this problem (numba, Kronecker-sum\n  H·v, rung spin-flip terms; `analysis/ed_hubbard.py`, `ed_bilayer.py`). It was verified against free fermions,\n  the two-site Hubbard model, and rung-singlet product states.\n  * Single-layer attractive Hubbard model: periodic clusters of 10 (√10×√10), 16 (4×4) and 20 (√20×√20) sites.\n  * Bilayer model: periodic 16-site cluster (8 rungs, √8×√8), Hilbert-space dimension up to 1.66×10⁸.\n  * Quantities: gaps (E(N+1)+E(N−1)−2E(N))/2, spin gaps E(S_z=1)−E(S_z=0), and phase stiffness from twisted\n    boundary conditions.\n* **Cluster perturbation theory (CPT).** Open bilayer clusters of 8 (2×2×2), 12 (3×2×2) and 16 (4×2×2) sites.\n  The cluster Green's function comes from a band (block) Lanczos method, checked against an exact Lehmann sum\n  to 10⁻¹³. It is coupled through the in-plane inter-cluster hopping and periodized\n  (`analysis/cpt_bilayer.py`, `cpt_analyze.py`). Non-square clusters are orientation-averaged. CPT is exact at\n  U = J⊥ = 0, which was checked. The 16-site half-filled cluster (Hilbert space 1.66×10⁸) exceeds the 32 GiB memory of the workstation\n  container with an 8-vector block. It was therefore split with the mirror y → 1−y into even/odd 4×4 blocks\n  (`analysis/cpt_half16_lean.py`), which reproduces the full block Lanczos to 10⁻⁷ on the 8-site cluster. Doped\n  CPT: 16-site clusters with 6 and 10 electrons (ν = 0.1875, 0.3125).\n* **Exact cluster Green's function.** G(K, ω) of the periodic 16-site bilayer at its allowed momenta (Γ, X, M,\n  (½,½)/2) by Lanczos continued fractions (`analysis/ed_bilayer_gk.py`). This is a CPT-independent check of the\n  sign structure of G at midgap.\n* **Mean field.** BCS for interlayer singlet pairing driven by J⊥ (`analysis/bcs_bilayer.py`), with a 256×256\n  k-grid and density fixed by the number equation.\n* **Two-body problem.** Exact pair binding energy of the attractive model on the infinite lattice (1024² k-grid).\n* **Data fits.** Weighted least squares. The quoted errors are from the covariance, rescaled by χ²/dof when\n  > 1. The NMR error bars in the file are conservative (χ²/dof ≈ 0.15 for good fits).\n\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## 9. Limitations\n\n* A bilayer block is *inferred* (from LSM plus the data), not stated in the problem. It is the most economical\n  structure that allows the observed featureless gapped state with the observed (large) spin gap.\n* A large J⊥ with t⊥ ≈ 0 requires the interlayer exchange to be transmitted by other orbitals (apical O,\n  d_{z²}-like admixture), not by hopping within the active band.\n* The transition temperatures of the doped crystals are mean-field-like (T_c(0.2) = T_MF). A strictly 2D model\n  would give T_KT ≲ 0.3 at ν = 0.2. The measured T_c therefore implies three-dimensional coupling between\n  bilayers, which the in-plane model does not describe. The T_c dome between the measured points is schematic.\n* At the representative parameters the model's spin gap (4.7) is about 15% below the NMR value (5.5 ± 0.5). Raising\n  J⊥ to fit it would overshoot the doped gaps by a similar amount. Finite clusters also overestimate the doped\n  gaps (ED: 2.45 vs 1.96 at ν ≈ 0.2). The finite-cluster CPT of the doped crystals does not resolve the\n  high-energy two-scale structure of STS (b), which is therefore taken from the data (§6).\n* The size of the M-pocket of zeros (Task 5) depends on the k-dependent self-energy and moves somewhat with\n  cluster size (0.914 → 0.871 → 0.855 for 8, 12, 16 sites, converging). The qualitative result (Γ side ≫ ν, a small closed curve\n  around M, exactly ½ when t′ = 0) is robust.\n\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## 10. It lacks particle–hole symmetry because of t′.\n   - **State at half filling:** every vertical pair holds one spin singlet. Nothing is broken and the state is not topologically ordered.\n2. **Phase diagram.** Interlayer s± superconducting domes on both sides of ν = 1/2, a preformed-pair pseudogap region below T*, and the singlet insulator at ν = 1/2.
